problem: The exact-source production snapshot acquired a Netlify MCP proxy via OIDC but the actual upload failed with HTTP 401 Unauthorized, while the linked build trigger also returned ok=false.
root_cause: The production deploy transport can hold an unusable or expired proxy authorization even when bridge acquisition itself succeeds. Transport acquisition success was therefore not equivalent to upload authorization.
prevention: Treat HTTP 401 from Netlify exact-source upload as a transport-auth failure, never as an application or i18n failure.
When the linked Netlify integration is available, a bounded website-source trigger may activate the Git-linked build without relying on the failed upload proxy.
Keep exact production commit_ref and browser state-change proof mandatory after any fallback.
Never mark LIVE from a ready stale deployment.
Persist the 401 transport failure and recovery path in Brain, ledger, docs and continuity skill.
Reacquire GitHub OIDC and a fresh Netlify bridge proxy inside every bounded exact-source upload attempt.
Retry only an explicit provider 401 Unauthorized; all non-auth transport failures remain fail-closed.
A successful retry must still prove exact production commit_ref and browser readback before LIVE.

evidence.failed_step: Deploy exact source through authorized Netlify transport

repeat_evidence_2026_10_04.previous_prevention_gap: Proxy refresh occurred only once immediately before upload; first upload still failed and required a separate workflow retry.
repeat_evidence_2026_10_04.structural_fix: Acquire fresh GitHub OIDC token and Netlify bridge proxy inside each bounded exact-source upload attempt; retry only provider 401; fail closed for other transport errors.
